Summary: Learner onboarding and learning plans
Description: UC1 and UC2: account, conversational profile, learning portrait and personalised weekly plans by the Learning Coordinator.

Summary: UC1 Register and create learner profile
Description: As a working professional I can create an account and a learner profile (exam, level, target, exam date, weekly hours, priority skills) so the platform can personalise my study.
Acceptance Criteria: Sign-up needs only name, email and password | Profile fields are validated | Profile can be edited later | Passwords are hashed and sessions use JWT

Summary: Registration, login and profile API with database tables
Description: FastAPI endpoints, SQLAlchemy models and Alembic migration for users and profiles.

Summary: Test invalid profile input and duplicate emails
Conversational onboarding assistant
Description: The Learning Coordinator interviews the learner by voice or text and fills the profile one question at a time.
Acceptance Criteria: Assistant asks for each missing field | Answers can be typed or spoken | Learner confirms the draft before it is saved

Summary: Learning portrait
Description: After onboarding the Coordinator writes a quality-checked portrait: goal, starting point, focus areas, study rhythm and next steps.
Acceptance Criteria: Portrait never claims measured strengths without verified results | Portrait passes the quality gate

Summary: UC2 Create and accept a personalised learning plan
Description: The Coordinator proposes weekly activities with a rationale; the learner accepts, rejects or requests changes.
Acceptance Criteria: Plan lists priorities, activities, minutes and reasons | Accepting activates the plan and creates study tasks | 'More speaking' style change requests move that skill up | Only released plans can be accepted

Summary: Coordinator LangGraph workflow and hand-offs
Description: StateGraph: Coordinator -> Quality Manager -> release or human wait.

Summary: Account recovery
Description: One-time password reset by email or on-screen link for local use.
Acceptance Criteria: Reset token works once | Existing sessions are revoked after reset

Summary: Email verification at sign-up
Description: Remaining gap from the implementation status: verify the email address before activating an account.
Acceptance Criteria: Unverified accounts cannot start a plan | Verification link expires

Summary: Four-skill practice with the AI Tutor
Description: UC3 and UC4 plus listening, reading, the AI Tutor with memory and the learner notebooks.

Summary: UC3 Live speaking test with an AI examiner
Description: The avatar examiner speaks every question aloud and listens through the microphone: IELTS Part 1 -> Part 2 cue card (1 min prep, 2 min talk) -> Part 3, or TOEFL Listen & Repeat + Interview.
Acceptance Criteria: Hands-free turn-taking | Real timers for preparation and talk | Session audio recorded for replay | Feedback on fluency, vocabulary and grammar | Pronunciation is never scored from a transcript

Summary: Speaking examiner state machine and speech services
Description: examiner.py stages, browser speech recognition with optional cloud transcription and text-to-speech.

Summary: Test that all three IELTS parts run in order
UC4 Writing practice with trustworthy feedback
Description: Task 1 with charts, Task 2, TOEFL email and academic discussion; criterion scores, sentence-level corrections, rewrites and comparison with the previous attempt.
Acceptance Criteria: Timer and word count | Every comment quotes the sentence and gives a fix | Bands for all four criteria | Resubmission shows issues fixed, issues remaining and criterion changes

Summary: Rubric analyser and writing editor
Description: Local rubric analyser (scoring.py), autosaved drafts and revision history.

Summary: Listening practice in real exam format
Description: IELTS Parts 1-4 and TOEFL tasks with multi-speaker audio, played once in exam mode; marked against hidden keys with band conversion and transcript evidence.

Summary: Reading practice in real exam format
Description: TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN, matching headings, MCQ and completion; TOEFL Complete-the-Words; timer and evidence highlighting.

Summary: AI Tutor with long-term memory
Description: Full-page tutor and floating assistant that remember the learner's background, goals, difficulties and verified progress; 'Coach me' daily plan.
Acceptance Criteria: Memories persist across conversations | Learner can view and delete memories | Tutor uses notebook statistics in its advice

Summary: Mistake, Word, Grammar and Sentence books
Description: Notebooks fed by every skill: wrong answers by question type, saved words with phonetics and Chinese meaning, grammar errors and advanced sentences, with spaced review.
Acceptance Criteria: Selecting any word saves it | Telling the tutor 'I don't know the word ...' saves it | Statistics show the most-missed question types | Flashcards and 'quiz me' review

Summary: Test-mode word lock
Description: During tests and mocks a selected word can be saved but its meaning stays hidden; the dictionary and tutor are locked server-side.
Acceptance Criteria: Meaning hidden while a test is running | Full meaning shown after the test

Summary: Inline prose diff between writing attempts
Description: Remaining gap: show sentence-level differences between two drafts.
Acceptance Criteria: Changed sentences are highlighted

Summary: Acoustic pronunciation assessment
Description: Remaining gap: score pronunciation from audio rather than transcripts.
Acceptance Criteria: Pronunciation score uses audio features and is clearly labelled

Summary: Assessment, mock exams and analytics
Description: UC5 and UC6: four-section mock exams, consistent scoring, performance reports and readiness.

Summary: UC5 Take a four-section mock examination
Description: Short (~90 min) or full (~2 h 45 min) computer-delivered mock: listening played once, three reading passages, both writing tasks and the live speaking examiner.
Acceptance Criteria: Persistent timer and autosave | Can resume after closing the browser | Section scores and overall estimate | Requires an accepted plan

Summary: Distinguish IELTS bands and TOEFL 2026 1-6 scale
Description: Raw score -> band tables for IELTS; proportion -> 1-6 for TOEFL.

Summary: UC6 Performance report and weaknesses
Description: Verified-only skill charts, history, strengths, weaknesses, repeated issues and readiness, with a quality-checked narrative.
Acceptance Criteria: Only released results are counted | Report passes the quality gate

Summary: Knowledge graph of skills and issues
Description: Interactive graph linking skills, question types and repeated issues.

Summary: Validate band conversion against official papers
Description: Remaining gap: compare our conversion with released official practice papers.
Acceptance Criteria: Conversion differences are documented

Summary: Plan adaptation, human review and teacher console
Description: UC7 and UC8: weekly adaptation from verified progress, instructor review of held results, anomaly detection and learner reports.

Summary: UC7 Receive an adapted learning plan
Description: Manual and scheduled weekly adaptation using verified progress; the learner accepts or rejects and the active plan is preserved.
Acceptance Criteria: Adaptation uses Assessment insights | Active plan stays until the new one is accepted | Weekly run is idempotent

Summary: Weekly adaptation trigger
Description: scheduled_review.py for cron / Task Scheduler.

Summary: UC8 Review an escalated case
Description: The instructor sees evidence and confidence for each held result and can approve, correct or request information; decisions are audited.
Acceptance Criteria: Only the instructor role can review | Corrections are validated against the exam scale | Approved results are released to the learner

Summary: Teacher developer console
Description: Instructor-only console: agent activity trace, per-agent latency, engine mode and activity charts.
Acceptance Criteria: Learners cannot see agent activity | Trace filters by agent, learner and slow steps

Summary: Anomaly detection and learner problem reports
Description: Model failures, provider outages, holds, hold-rate trends, latency, speech failures, score drops, curriculum gaps and inactivity; learners can report a wrong score and get a reply.
Acceptance Criteria: Each anomaly can be acknowledged | Learner reports appear in the console and replies reach the learner

Summary: Deployed scheduler, multi-instructor assignment and notifications
Description: Remaining gaps for UC7 and UC8.
Acceptance Criteria: Weekly job runs without manual start | Cases can be assigned | Instructor is notified

Summary: Quality gate, materials and agent platform
Description: UC9 and UC10 plus the shared LLM adapter, per-agent memory and tools.

Summary: UC9 Check agent output quality
Description: Every result passes structure, threshold, rubric-key, score-range and consistency checks; failures are held and escalated.
Acceptance Criteria: Learners only see RELEASED results | Confidence below threshold is held | Score/feedback contradictions are held | Threshold is adjustable and audited

Summary: Test the release invariant
UC10 Recommended study materials
Description: Ranked materials with a reason for each, based on weaknesses, quality-checked like feedback.
Acceptance Criteria: Learners without results get starter materials | 'Not relevant' feedback affects ranking

Summary: Exam-format question bank and AI generation
Description: Structured IELTS/TOEFL bank with AI generation; generated tests are validated (every completion answer must appear in the script/passage).

Summary: Per-agent memory and tools
Description: Each of the four agents has its own memory and read-only tools; the model chooses tools in a bounded loop and submits structured output.
Acceptance Criteria: Coordinator, Tutor, Assessment and Quality each have their own tools | Tool calls are logged | Teacher can view agent memory | Instructor decisions become Quality Manager lessons

Summary: Cloud model configuration (GPT-6 Luna)
Description: One ProviderAdapter for all model calls; GPT-6 Luna via the Responses API with reasoning effort none/low; offline LOCAL engine when no key.
Acceptance Criteria: Placeholder key keeps LOCAL mode | Provider can be changed in .env

Summary: Live test of the cloud agents with a real API key
Description: Run the agents end to end with GPT-6 Luna and record results.
Acceptance Criteria: Chat, feedback, plan and quality verdict work in REAL mode | Costs and latency recorded

Summary: Measure quality-gate false positives and negatives
Description: Remaining gap for UC9 (target: about 1 in 50 false alarms).
Acceptance Criteria: Rates measured on a labelled sample

Summary: Pixel-art experience, deployment and evidence
Description: User interface, Docker deployment, automated tests, documentation and submission evidence.

Summary: Surreal animated pixel-art interface
Description: Animated pixel world, switchable witch (Luna) or boy (Kai) companion that talks, smooth page and dialog animations.

Summary: Docker deployment that runs from a fresh clone
Description: docker compose up --build serves the app on port 8080 without any .env; migrations and seed run at startup.
Acceptance Criteria: Fresh clone starts with no extra steps | API keys never committed

Summary: Automated tests and CI
Description: pytest backend suite, Playwright browser tests and GitHub Actions.

Summary: README, implementation status and Canvas package
Description: Clear setup guide, use-case status table and a script that builds the submission zip.

Summary: Final demo, sprint reviews and submission
Description: Record the demo, complete sprint review and retrospective evidence, submit by 1 November.
Acceptance Criteria: Video recorded | Four sprint reviews filled in | Zip submitted
